title: POV: YOU Owe $14,000 and Are Debt Free in 29 Months — Jake Is Still Paying for 7 Years
description:
Debt snowball vs debt avalanche: which way to pay off debt fast actually wins? You owe $14,000 (a medical bill, a car loan and a credit card at 25%), and tonight you run the real numbers on three plans.

In this POV story, Jake pays only the minimums: about 7.5 years and roughly $9,500 in interest. Mia uses the debt snowball (smallest balance first): debt free in 30 months, about $3,800 in interest. You use the debt avalanche (highest interest first): debt free in 29 months, about $2,900 in interest. Plus how you find $170 extra a month, and how to pick the method you'll actually finish.

⏱️ CHAPTERS
0:00 The Debt Pile
0:39 The Minimum Trap
1:11 Finding $170
1:39 The Snowball
2:07 The Avalanche
2:47 Head to Head
3:12 Which One Wins
3:40 29 Months Later

💬 Are you team snowball or team avalanche? Tell me in the comments!
👍 Subscribe to Simple Money Life for a new simple money move every day.

Numbers are an example with fixed minimum payments ($50, $200, $180) and $600 a month in total; your own loans and rates will differ.

⚠️ This video is for educational purposes only and is not financial advice.

short2.title: POV: Christmas Is 8 Weeks Away… and Your $600 Is Already Saved 🎄
short2.description: Christmas is on the same day every year, so save for it like a bill: a sinking fund. $50 a month from January = $600 by December. Starting late? $40 a week for 8 weeks = $320. Same Christmas, no credit card debt in January.
